newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwean in divine plea over telephone blues.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwean in divine plea over telephone blues.

text.p: A Zimbabwean management training consultant frustrated over the lack of a working telephone has turned to God to deal with evil spirits he claims are responsible for his communication troubles.

Clifford Mashiri of Aquarius Training Services said the company's Harare telephone had not been working since June, and the state-owned Posts and Telecommunications Corporation (PTC) had not responded to their pleas to get it tinkling again.
"Having exhausted all earthly options, I hereby make a prayer for divine intervention:

"Our Father who art in Heaven, hear us this day. Ward off all evil spirits that are blocking our way to getting telephone services from the PTC. Inspire the PTC to transfer our telephone 750250 and give us another line today. Amen," he said in a letter to a local newspaper.

PTC officials were unavailable for comment on Thursday, but over the months, the state monopoly has been saying its service -- which was described last year by a local judge as notoriously inefficient -- is improving.
It says it can connect individuals within a year and companies within three months. But the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) says the average all-round wait is three years to get a phone.
An average of five companies advertise in Zimbabwe's dominant state media daily, advising clients and business contacts that their telephones are out of order or difficult to get through.
